Technical Report: Statistical, Numerical, and Algorithmic Modifications in the HallquistLab/pTFCE Fork

Tracking Departures from Upstream spisakt/pTFCE (v0.2.2.1)

Author

Hallquist Lab

Published

November 20, 2026

1 Overview & Motivation

Probabilistic Threshold-Free Cluster Enhancement (pTFCE), introduced by Spisák et al. (2019, NeuroImage, 185, 12–26), integrates multi-threshold cluster-extent information into voxelwise neuroimaging inference via Bayes’ rule and Gaussian Random Field (GRF) theory. Unlike standard TFCE (Smith & Nichols, 2009), pTFCE outputs calibrated probabilities and \(Z\)-scores directly without requiring computationally expensive permutation testing.

While applying pTFCE extensively to group-level fMRI analyses—particularly bi-sided (two-tailed) contrasts where both positive activations and negative deactivations are of scientific interest—we identified several interacting mathematical, numerical, and software issues in upstream spisakt/pTFCE (v0.2.2.1, commit 6fd6be5):

  1. Cross-tail and cross-cluster threshold grid interference: Fixing the threshold count Nh = 100 across [0, logpmax] causes the integration step size \(\Delta h \propto \frac{1}{2}Z_{\max}^2\) to depend on the global maximum \(Z\)-score in each tail. Strong focal peaks in one tail coarsen \(\Delta h\) by 15–35\(\times\) relative to a moderate opposite tail, shifting enhanced \(Z\)-scores of unrelated clusters across the FWER significance boundary and crashing with Inf when \(Z_{\max} > 37.5\).
  2. Catastrophic nested quadrature failures (p > 1, cluster-border NaNs, and silent interior score deflation): Evaluating the Bayes normalization integral via stats::integrate(..., -Inf, Inf) inside pvox.clust() misses narrow posterior spikes near \(Z_{\text{estThr}} = 1.3\) when smoothness is low/moderate (\(R_d\) large) and cluster size \(c\) is large, returning “probabilities” \(> 1\) (up to \(10^{19}\)), producing NaNs on cluster borders (upstream Issues #8, #10, #25) and silently deflating interior cluster \(Z\)-scores.
  3. A ~20% zero “dead zone” around \(Z = 0\) and -8.2095 background floor: Discrete left-endpoint summation below ZestThr maps small positive \(|Z|\) values to \(p > 0.5\) (\(Z_{\text{pTFCE}} < 0\)), collapsing ~20% of in-mask voxels to 0 under standard two-pass clamping and mapping out-of-mask/opposite-tail voxels to -8.209536 (Issues #11, #16, #24).
  4. Unmasked connected-component leakage & R \(\ge\) 4.2 incompatibilities: mmand::components() ran prior to masking (allowing clusters and max(img) to bleed outside ROI masks), if (!is.na(residual)) threw a fatal error on R \(\ge\) 4.2 for 4D residual arrays, interpolate() returned NaN (0/0) at exact DOF lookup knots and used an inverted linear interpolation endpoint, and pure-R loops required ~2.5–5 minutes and 1.5–4 GB of RAM per whole-brain bi-sided contrast.

This document records all statistical, numerical, algorithmic, and API departures introduced in HallquistLab/pTFCE (v0.3.0+) relative to upstream spisakt/pTFCE (v0.2.2.1), alongside executable demonstrations.

3 Bi-Sided (+Z and -Z) Improvements

library(pTFCE)
library(RNifti)
library(ggplot2)

3.1 Eliminating Non-Local Z_max Interference & Tail Asymmetry

In upstream pTFCE, Nh = 100 thresholds are spaced evenly from 0 to \(\text{logpmax} = -\log\Phi(-Z_{\max}) \approx \frac{1}{2}Z_{\max}^2\). Whenever one tail contains a strong focal peak (e.g., \(Z_{\max}^+ = 25\) in visual or motor cortex, giving \(\Delta h^+ \approx 3.20\)) while the opposite tail has moderate peaks (\(Z_{\max}^- = 4.5\), giving \(\Delta h^- \approx 0.13\)), the two tails use vastly different integration step sizes, and moderate clusters in the strong-peak tail lose most of their cluster-forming thresholds. Furthermore, upstream pnorm(max(img), lower.tail = FALSE) underflowed to 0 at \(Z_{\max} > 37.5\), crashing seq() with 'to' must be a finite number.

In HallquistLab/pTFCE, the Continuous + Fixed-dh default (dh = 0.05, legacy = FALSE) uses a fixed \(-\log p\) step size independent of \(Z_{\max}\) up to \(-\log p = 100\) (\(Z \approx 14\)), with bounded adaptive panels above \(-\log p = 100\):

d <- c(24L, 24L, 24L)
mask <- array(1, dim = d)
base_img <- array(0, dim = d)
# Fixed target cluster in region A: 5x5x5 cube of Z = 3.6 with center 3.9
base_img[3:7, 3:7, 3:7] <- 3.6
base_img[5, 5, 5] <- 3.9

distant_peaks <- c(3.9, 6, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 36, 45)
records <- lapply(distant_peaks, function(z_dist) {
  img <- base_img
  img[20:21, 20:21, 20:21] <- min(z_dist, 15)
  img[20, 20, 20] <- z_dist

  # Fork default: fixed dh = 0.05 + analytical sub-ZestThr
  z_fixed <- ptfce(img, mask, V = prod(d), Rd = 1500, resels = 50,
                   sided = "positive", dh = 0.05, verbose = FALSE)$Z[5, 5, 5]

  # Legacy grid: fixed Nh = 100 (using log-space pnorm so Z = 45 doesn't crash)
  z_legacy <- ptfce(img, mask, V = prod(d), Rd = 1500, resels = 50,
                    sided = "positive", Nh = 100, legacy = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)$Z[5, 5, 5]

  data.frame(
    distant_Z_max = z_dist,
    `Fork default (dh = 0.05)` = z_fixed,
    `Legacy grid (Nh = 100)` = z_legacy,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
})
df_peak <- do.call(rbind, records)
df_long <- reshape(
  df_peak,
  varying = c("Fork default (dh = 0.05)", "Legacy grid (Nh = 100)"),
  v.names = "enhanced_Z",
  timevar = "Method",
  times = c("Fork default (dh = 0.05)", "Legacy grid (Nh = 100)"),
  direction = "long"
)

ggplot(df_long, aes(x = distant_Z_max, y = enhanced_Z, color = Method, shape = Method)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = fwe.p2z(prod(d) / 50, 0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  annotate("text", x = 36, y = fwe.p2z(prod(d) / 50, 0.05) + 0.08,
           label = "FWER p < 0.05 threshold", size = 3.3, color = "grey30") +
  labs(
    title = "Sensitivity of a Fixed Cluster (Peak Z = 3.9) to an Unrelated Distant Peak",
    x = "Distant Peak Z_max Elsewhere in Brain",
    y = "Enhanced pTFCE Z at Target Cluster [5,5,5]"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

3.2 Analytical Sub-ZestThr Integration & Removal of the Zero Dead-Zone

In the continuous limit \(\Delta h \to 0\), Spisák et al.’s equidistant logarithmic probability aggregation converges to: \[-\log p_{\text{pTFCE}}(v) = \sqrt{2 \int_0^{x_v} \left(-\log P\big(H > h(x) \mid C = c_v(h(x))\big)\right) dx}, \qquad x_v = -\log\Phi(-|Z_v|)\] Because GRF cluster theory does not apply below ZestThr = 1.3 (\(x_{\text{ZestThr}} = -\log\Phi(-1.3) \approx 2.3351\)), \(P(H > h(x) \mid C)\) equals the unenhanced tail probability \(e^{-x}\) for all \(x \le x_{\text{ZestThr}}\). Thus the sub-threshold integral is analytically exact: \[\int_0^{\min(x_v, x_{\text{ZestThr}})} x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\min(x_v, x_{\text{ZestThr}})^2\]

Evaluating this lower segment analytically ensures \(\tilde{Z}_v = Z_v\) identically for all \(|Z_v| \le 1.3\), eliminating both unnecessary connected-component sweeps below \(Z = 1.3\) and the ~20% zero dead-zone around \(Z = 0\) seen when clamping two legacy one-sided runs:

z_path <- system.file("extdata", "test03B_zstat1.nii.gz", package = "pTFCE")
m_path <- system.file("extdata", "test03B_mask.nii.gz", package = "pTFCE")
z_nii <- readNifti(z_path)
m_nii <- readNifti(m_path)
inside <- as.array(m_nii) > 0.5
z_raw <- as.array(z_nii)[inside]

sm <- smoothest(z_nii, m_nii, verbose = FALSE)
V <- sm$volume
Rd <- sm$dLh * V

# 1. Native bi-sided (fork default)
bi_modern <- ptfce(z_nii, m_nii, Rd = Rd, V = V, resels = sm$resels,
                   sided = "two.sided", verbose = FALSE)
z_modern <- as.array(bi_modern$Z)[inside]

# 2. Legacy two-pass wrapper behavior (Nh = 100 per tail, clamp Z < 0 to 0)
pos_leg <- ptfce(z_nii, m_nii, Rd = Rd, V = V, resels = sm$resels,
                 Nh = 100, legacy = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
neg_leg <- ptfce(-as.array(z_nii), as.array(m_nii), Rd = Rd, V = V, resels = sm$resels,
                 Nh = 100, legacy = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
z_leg_bi <- pmax(as.array(pos_leg$Z)[inside], 0) - pmax(as.array(neg_leg$Z)[inside], 0)

cat(sprintf("In-mask voxels equal to exact 0:\n  Raw Z-map:        %.2f%%\n  Legacy 2-pass:    %.2f%%\n  Fork two.sided:   %.2f%%\n",
            100 * mean(z_raw == 0), 100 * mean(z_leg_bi == 0), 100 * mean(z_modern == 0)))
In-mask voxels equal to exact 0:
  Raw Z-map:        11.11%
  Legacy 2-pass:    20.26%
  Fork two.sided:   11.11%
set.seed(1)
samp <- sample(which(abs(z_raw) < 3.5), 4000)
df_map <- rbind(
  data.frame(raw_Z = z_raw[samp], enh_Z = z_leg_bi[samp], Mode = "Legacy 2-pass (Nh = 100 + zero clamp)"),
  data.frame(raw_Z = z_raw[samp], enh_Z = z_modern[samp], Mode = "Fork native sided = 'two.sided' (dh = 0.05)")
)

ggplot(df_map, aes(x = raw_Z, y = enh_Z, color = Mode)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "black") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ Mode) +
  labs(
    title = "Input vs. Enhanced Z-Scores Across [-3.5, 3.5] on Whole-Brain fMRI Z-Map",
    x = "Original Input Z",
    y = "Enhanced Bi-Sided pTFCE Z"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

3.3 Bi-Sided Return Conventions

When sided = "two.sided":

  • $Z: Signed enhanced \(Z\)-scores (> 0 where input \(Z > 0\), < 0 where input \(Z < 0\), 0 outside mask), satisfying strict contrast anti-symmetry ptfce(-Z, mask, sided = "two.sided")$Z == -ptfce(Z, mask, sided = "two.sided")$Z.
  • $p and $logp: Two-sided uncorrected enhanced \(p\)-values \(p_{\text{2s}} = \min(1, 2 p_{\text{1s}}) = 2\Phi(-|\tilde{Z}|)\) and \(-\log p_{\text{2s}}\).
  • $fwer0.05.Z and $fwe.Z: Two-sided GRF FWER thresholds computed at \(\alpha / 2\) per tail (fwe.p2z(number_of_resels, fwe_p / 2)), so thresholding at abs(res$Z) >= res$fwer0.05.Z controls two-sided family-wise error rate at \(\alpha = 0.05\).

4 Numerical Stability: Log-Space Posterior Quadrature

4.1 Diagnosis of Upstream NaN and Underflow Bugs

Upstream pTFCE computed \(P(H > \text{actH} \mid C = c, H \ge Z_{\text{estThr}})\) via two nested calls to stats::integrate:

# Upstream R/ptfce.r (v0.2.2.1):
dvox.clust <- function(h, V, Rd, c, ZestThr = 1.3) {
  dvox(h) * dclust(h, V, Rd, c, ZestThr) /
    stats::integrate(function(x) dvox(x) * dclust(x, V, Rd, c, ZestThr), -Inf, Inf)$value
}
pvox.clust <- function(V, Rd, c, actH, ZestThr = 1.3) {
  stats::integrate(function(x) dvox.clust(x, V, Rd, c, ZestThr = ZestThr), actH, Inf)$value
}

When image smoothness is low/moderate (\(R_d = V \cdot \text{dLh}\) large) and a cluster at low thresholds is large (\(c\) large), the unnormalized density \(f(x) = \phi(x)\lambda(x)\exp(-\lambda(x)c^{2/3})\) concentrates in a very narrow spike just above \(x = 1.3\). Mapping (-Inf, Inf) via QUADPACK’s transformation missed most of that spike in the denominator while integrate(..., actH, Inf) captured it in the numerator—producing pvox.clust > 1 (e.g., \(1.01 \times 10^{19}\) at \(V = 300\text{k}, R_d = 100\text{k}, c = 20\text{k}, h = 1.31\), i.e. \(-\log p = -43.76\)). Border voxels with no higher-threshold contributions then yielded \(8s + \Delta h < 0 \implies \texttt{NaN}\) inside sqrt(), while interior cluster voxels had 43.76 silently subtracted from their \(-\log p\) sum without triggering a warning.

4.2 Strict Concavity & Mode-Shifted Gauss-Kronrod Solution

In src/ptfce_core.cpp, we work entirely with the log-unnormalized posterior on \((1.1, \infty)\): \[\ell(h) = -\frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi) - \frac{h^2}{2} + \log\lambda(h) - c^{2/3}\lambda(h)\]

  1. Analytical cancellation in Mill’s ratio: For \(h \ge 12\), \(\log\Phi(-h) + \frac{1}{2}h^2\) is evaluated via a 32-term Laplace continued fraction, avoiding IEEE double underflow of \(\Phi(-h)\) for \(h > 38\) and avoiding \(\frac{1}{2}h^2 - \frac{1}{2}h^2\) cancellation.
  2. Guaranteed unimodality: All three terms of \(\ell(h)\) have strictly negative second derivative (\(\ell''(h) < 0\)) on \((1.1, \infty)\). Thus \(\ell(h)\) has a unique global maximum \(m^* \ge a\) on any \([a, \infty)\), found via derivative sign check at \(a\) plus golden-section search, and decays monotonically past \(m^*\) to \(b\) where \(\ell(b) = \ell(m^*) - 50\) (\(e^{-50} \approx 1.9 \times 10^{-22}\)).
  3. Adaptive 15-point Gauss-Kronrod + log1p near ZestThr: Integrating \(\exp(\ell(x) - \ell(m^*)) \in [0, 1]\) on \([a, m^*]\) and \([m^*, b]\) achieves \(< 10^{-12}\) relative accuracy, caches \(\log I_{\text{den}}(c)\) once per unique integer cluster size \(c\), and switches to \(\text{log1p}(I_{\text{left}} / I_{\text{num}})\) whenever \(\log I_{\text{den}} - \log I_{\text{num}} < 0.05\), guaranteeing \(0 < p \le 1\) strictly:
cases <- expand.grid(
  Rd = c(2000, 50000, 100000),
  c_size = c(500, 20000),
  h = c(1.31, 4.50)
)
cases$neglog_p <- mapply(
  function(rd, cs, hh) pTFCE:::neglog_pvox_clust_cpp(300000, rd, cs, hh, 1.3),
  cases$Rd, cases$c_size, cases$h
)
cases$p_val <- exp(-cases$neglog_p)
knitr::kable(cases, digits = 5,
             caption = "Exact log-space posterior -log(p) across regimes where upstream v0.2.2.1 overflowed (p > 1 -> NaN) or underflowed (capped at 745).")

5 Masking, Smoothness, & Bug Fixes

  1. Strict pre-masking & SPM NaN hygiene: ptfce() now thresholds inside = mask > 0.5 and zeros img[!inside] <- 0 before checking for NA/Inf, computing z_peak, or running connected components. Out-of-mask NaNs (standard in SPM spmT images) no longer trigger false warnings, and supra-threshold features outside an ROI mask can never merge with in-mask voxels.
  2. Smoothness estimation on bi-sided maps & 4D residuals:
    • Fixed if (!is.na(residual)) so passing a 4D residual image directly to ptfce() works on R \(\ge\) 4.2.
    • Fixed 3D images stored with 4th dimension 1 (dim = c(nx, ny, nz, 1)) so smoothest() treats them as 3D rather than crashing in aperm() (upstream Issue #19).
    • Fixed interpolate(v) in smoothest(), which previously divided 0 / 0 = NaN whenever dof equaled an exact lookup knot (5..20, 25, 30, 40, 50, ...) and added + j.second instead of + i.second during linear interpolation.
    • Note on Z-map smoothness: when 4D residuals are unavailable, smoothness is always estimated on the full unrectified signed \(Z\)-map inside the mask. Zeroing negative voxels prior to smoothest() severely biases resel estimates (e.g., 467.2 vs 693.4 resels on test03B_zstat1.nii.gz, a 33% bias).
  3. Exact vectorized fwe.p2z() and fwe.z2p(): Replaced scalar 0.001-tolerance bisection with vectorized log-space Newton-Raphson inversion (1e-13 relative tolerance), maintaining exact mutual inversion (fwe.z2p(r, fwe.p2z(r, alpha)) == alpha) even for extreme \(\alpha < 10^{-100}\).

6 Non-Stationary Smoothness Adjustment (v0.4.0, Opt-In)

6.1 Theory & Regularized Voxelwise Roughness Estimation

Standard pTFCE assumes spatially stationary smoothness across the entire mask, measuring every cluster by its raw voxel count \(c = |\mathcal{C}|\). In real group fMRI, smoothness varies substantially across anatomy (e.g., medial prefrontal and posterior cingulate cortex are often 2–3\(\times\) smoother than subcortical nuclei, brainstem, or cerebellum; Hayasaka et al., 2004; Eklund et al., 2016).

Following Worsley et al. (1999) and Salimi-Khorshidi et al. (2011), setting nonstationary = TRUE (while leaving nonstationary = FALSE as the default) replaces raw voxel count \(c\) with local resel-scaled cluster size: \[\tilde{c}(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{C}} w(v), \qquad w(v) = \frac{\widehat{\text{dLh}}(v)}{\overline{\text{dLh}}}, \qquad \frac{1}{V}\sum_{v \in M} w(v) = 1\]

To prevent single-voxel derivative variance noise at finite degrees of freedom:

  1. smoothest(..., nonstationary = TRUE, smooth_fwhm = 3.0) accumulates symmetric forward and backward neighbor cross-products inside the mask during the same C++ pass over 4D res4d.
  2. Numerator and denominator sufficient statistics are smoothed separately via normalized within-mask separable 3D Gaussian convolution (smooth_fwhm = 3.0 voxels) with mild empirical-Bayes shrinkage (5% prior weight) toward the global directional correlation and winsorization to \(w(v) \in [0.02, 50.0]\).
  3. Rather than using the global pooled \(S_{-}/S_2\) ratio (which underestimates total search-volume resels under non-stationarity via Jensen’s inequality), smoothest() also computes the exact Worsley (1999) Riemannian roughness integral \(\text{dLh}_{\text{nonstationary}} = \frac{1}{V} \sum_{v \in M} \widehat{\text{dLh}}(v)\) (resels_nonstationary), which ptfce(..., nonstationary = TRUE) uses automatically.
  4. Inside ptfce_tail_cpp(), Disjoint-Set Union accumulates continuous cluster mass \(\tilde{c}(\mathcal{C})\) in \(O(1)\) per merge and evaluates log-space posteriors via 256-node / 64-node 4-point cubic Lagrange interpolation tables in \(\log \tilde{c}\).
  5. Precomputed smoothness lists (smoothest(..., nonstationary = TRUE)) or external RPV maps (e.g., SPM’s RPV.nii) can also be passed via local_smoothness = ... to avoid recomputing residual smoothness across multiple contrasts.
smooth_white <- function(x, sigma) {
  rad <- ceiling(3.5 * sigma)
  k <- exp(-0.5 * ((-rad:rad)^2) / (sigma^2)); k <- k / sqrt(sum(k^2))
  d <- dim(x); pd <- d + 2L * rad
  pad <- array(rnorm(prod(pd)), dim = pd)
  pad[(rad + 1):(rad + d[1]), (rad + 1):(rad + d[2]), (rad + 1):(rad + d[3])] <- x
  y1 <- array(0, dim = c(d[1], pd[2], pd[3]))
  for (i in seq_along(k)) y1 <- y1 + k[i] * pad[i:(i + d[1] - 1), , ]
  y2 <- array(0, dim = c(d[1], d[2], pd[3]))
  for (i in seq_along(k)) y2 <- y2 + k[i] * y1[, i:(i + d[2] - 1), ]
  y3 <- array(0, dim = d)
  for (i in seq_along(k)) y3 <- y3 + k[i] * y2[, , i:(i + d[3] - 1)]
  y3
}

set.seed(2026)
d_ns <- c(32L, 24L, 16L); nt_ns <- 30L; mask_ns <- array(1, dim = d_ns)
res4d_ns <- array(0, dim = c(d_ns, nt_ns))
for (t in seq_len(nt_ns)) {
  wn <- array(rnorm(prod(d_ns)), dim = d_ns)
  v_r <- smooth_white(wn, 0.75) # Left half (x <= 16): rough (subcortex-like)
  v_s <- smooth_white(wn, 2.00) # Right half (x >= 17): smooth (midline cortex-like)
  v_r[17:32, , ] <- v_s[17:32, , ]
  res4d_ns[, , , t] <- v_r
}

# Place two identical 3x3x3 clusters (Z = 3.4, center 3.7) in rough (x=8) vs smooth (x=24) halves
z_ns <- array(0, dim = d_ns)
z_ns[7:9, 11:13, 7:9]   <- 3.4; z_ns[8, 12, 8]  <- 3.7
z_ns[23:25, 11:13, 7:9] <- 3.4; z_ns[24, 12, 8] <- 3.7

out_st <- ptfce(z_ns, mask_ns, residual = res4d_ns, dof = nt_ns - 1,
                sided = "two.sided", nonstationary = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
out_ns <- ptfce(z_ns, mask_ns, residual = res4d_ns, dof = nt_ns - 1,
                sided = "two.sided", nonstationary = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)

df_prof <- rbind(
  data.frame(x = 1:32, Z = z_ns[, 12, 8], Curve = "1. Raw Input Z"),
  data.frame(x = 1:32, Z = out_st$Z[, 12, 8], Curve = "2. Stationary pTFCE (nonstationary = FALSE)"),
  data.frame(x = 1:32, Z = out_ns$Z[, 12, 8], Curve = "3. Non-Stationary pTFCE (nonstationary = TRUE)")
)

ggplot(df_prof, aes(x = x, y = Z, color = Curve, linetype = Curve)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 16.5, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = out_st$fwer0.05.Z, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 8.5, y = 5.25, label = "Rough Hemisphere\n(FWHM ~ 1.8 vox)", size = 3.3) +
  annotate("text", x = 24.5, y = 5.25, label = "Smooth Hemisphere\n(FWHM ~ 4.7 vox)", size = 3.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Identical 27-Voxel Clusters in Rough vs. Smooth Regions",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = analytical GRF two-sided FWER p < 0.05 threshold",
    x = "X Voxel Coordinate",
    y = "Z-Score along Line [x, 12, 8]"
  ) +
  ylim(-0.2, 5.6) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

7 Empirical FWER Threshold Calibration (v0.4.1): grf_sim vs. sign_flip

7.1 Why Classical Raw-Field GRF Thresholds Are Conservative on pTFCE Maps

Upstream pTFCE computes its Family-Wise Error Rate threshold (fwer0.05.Z) by plugging the unenhanced raw image’s resel count \(R = V / \text{resels}\) into the 3D Expected Euler Characteristic formula (fwe.p2z()). However, two mathematical properties of pTFCE make this raw-field analytical threshold substantially conservative:

  1. Topological smoothing of supra-threshold peaks: pTFCE aggregates cluster-extent beliefs across nested excursion sets, turning sharp voxelwise noise peaks into broader, smoother domes with far fewer effective local maxima than an unenhanced Gaussian field of roughness \(R_d\).
  2. Percolation conditioning at \(Z_{\text{estThr}} = 1.3\): Truncating the cluster-size likelihood below \(Z_{\text{estThr}}\) omits the unknown percolation factor \(P(H \ge Z_{\text{estThr}} \mid C) \le 1\), shifting moderate enhanced \(Z\)-scores slightly downward.

In realistic 3D group-fMRI Monte Carlo evaluations across anatomically heterogeneous smoothness zones (\(\text{FWHM} \in [3.0, 7.2]\) voxels), analytical fwe_method = "grf" yields an empirical two-sided FWER of only 0.010–0.015 at nominal \(\alpha = 0.05\) (fwer0.05.Z too high by \(\approx 0.30\text{–}0.38\) \(Z\)-units), sacrificing 35–55% of cluster detection sensitivity across all brain regions.

7.2 Two Empirical Calibration Solutions (fwe_method)

Version 0.4.1 keeps fwe_method = "grf" as the zero-overhead default while adding two fast C++ calibration engines (n_perm = 500L default) built atop a shared lazy 2D posterior lookup-table workspace (NullPtfceEngine):

  1. Parametric GRF Null Simulation (fwe_method = "grf_sim"):
    • Stationary mode (nonstationary = FALSE): Solves via bisection for 1D L2-unit discrete Gaussian kernels whose discrete lag-1 autocorrelation matches \(\exp(-1/(4\sigma_d^2))\) along \((x, y, z)\) and convolves 3D white noise over the tight padded bounding box of mask.
    • Non-stationary mode (nonstationary = TRUE): Synthesizes spatially varying smoothness via a \(K = 4\) multi-scale separable Gaussian filter bank driven by shared white noise across the \([0.5\%, 99.5\%]\) range of local log-scales \(u(v) = -\frac{1}{D}\log w(v)\), normalized at every voxel using the exact closed-form cross-scale filter inner product \(r_{k,k+1} = \prod_d \langle k_{d,k}, k_{d,k+1}\rangle\) so \(\text{Var}(Z_b(v)) \equiv 1\) everywhere inside mask.
    • Key advantage: Works directly from a single 3D \(Z\)-map (plus optional precomputed local_smoothness / RPV summary) with no 4D subject or residual volumes required.
  2. Rademacher Sign-Flipping Calibration (fwe_method = "sign_flip"):
    • 4D Subject Contrasts (copes supplied): Performs exact Rademacher (\(\pm 1\)) sign-flipping across \(M\) independent subject-level contrast maps using invariant precomputed sums of squares, transforming studentized one-sample \(t_{M-1}(v) \to Z_b(v)\) via a 512-node cubic spline + log-space tail transform. Supplying copes automatically selects fwe_method = "sign_flip" and estimates 4D smoothness if residual is omitted.
    • 4D GLM Residuals (residual supplied): Extracts an exact machine-precision orthonormal basis \(Q \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times \nu_{\text{sub}}}\) of the empirical GLM residual subspace via two-pass Modified Gram-Schmidt (automatically accounting for intercept and any regressed nuisance covariates without needing the design matrix \(X\)), projects Rademacher sign vectors onto \(\text{col}(Q)\), and maps pivotal \(t_{\nu_{\text{sub}}-1}(v) \to Z_b(v)\) via contiguous SIMD DAXPY sweeps. Also checks lag-1 autocorrelation along the 4th dimension and warns if unwhitened time-series TRs are supplied instead of exchangeable volumes.
    • Key advantage: 10–15\(\times\) faster than 3D multi-scale convolution on high-resolution whole-brain masks (~4–7 s at 301k voxels) while preserving empirical spatial covariance, non-stationarity, and non-Gaussian tail structure.

Both methods evaluate \(\max_{v \in M} \tilde{Z}_b(v)\) (or joint two-sided \(\max_{v \in M} |\tilde{Z}_b(v)|\) when sided = "two.sided") using only supra-\(Z_{\text{estThr}}\) candidate voxels and compute finite-sample exact order-statistic thresholds \(M_{(\lceil(1-\alpha)(B+1)\rceil)}\) (Phipson & Smyth, 2010).

set.seed(42)
cal_grf <- out_ns # analytical GRF from non-stationary demo above
cal_sim <- ptfce(z_ns, mask_ns, residual = res4d_ns, dof = nt_ns - 1,
                 sided = "two.sided", nonstationary = TRUE,
                 fwe_method = "grf_sim", n_perm = 199L, verbose = FALSE)
cal_sf  <- ptfce(z_ns, mask_ns, residual = res4d_ns, dof = nt_ns - 1,
                 sided = "two.sided", nonstationary = TRUE,
                 fwe_method = "sign_flip", n_perm = 199L, verbose = FALSE)

df_null <- rbind(
  data.frame(max_Z = cal_sim$null_max_Z, Method = "Parametric GRF Simulation (grf_sim)"),
  data.frame(max_Z = cal_sf$null_max_Z,  Method = "Rademacher Sign-Flipping (sign_flip)")
)
df_thr <- data.frame(
  Threshold = c(cal_grf$fwer0.05.Z, cal_sim$fwer0.05.Z, cal_sf$fwer0.05.Z),
  Label = c(
    sprintf("Analytical GRF (%.2f)", cal_grf$fwer0.05.Z),
    sprintf("grf_sim 95%% (%.2f)", cal_sim$fwer0.05.Z),
    sprintf("sign_flip 95%% (%.2f)", cal_sf$fwer0.05.Z)
  )
)

ggplot(df_null, aes(x = max_Z, fill = Method, color = Method)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.28, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = df_thr, aes(xintercept = Threshold, linetype = Label),
             color = c("#b22222", "#1b7837", "#2166ac"), linewidth = 0.95) +
  labs(
    title = "Null Distribution of max |Z_pTFCE| vs. Analytical Raw-Field GRF Threshold",
    subtitle = "Non-stationary two-sided pTFCE (B = 199 replicates; nominal alpha = 0.05)",
    x = "Maximum |Enhanced Z| Across Mask Under H0",
    y = "Density",
    linetype = "FWER 0.05 Threshold"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")

7.3 Monte Carlo Evaluation Across Realistic Group-fMRI Scenarios

We evaluated all FWER calibration modes across three 3D group-fMRI benchmarks (36 x 26 x 18 search volume spanning three anatomical smoothness zones: rough subcortex FWHM = 3.0, moderate lateral cortex FWHM = 4.8, and smooth medial DMN FWHM = 7.2 voxels; nominal two-sided \(\alpha = 0.05\), \(B = 199\) replicates per study):

Key takeaways from the head-to-head comparison:

  • Exact FWER recovery & substantial power gain: Both grf_sim (FWER = 0.045) and sign_flip (FWER = 0.050 on residuals, 0.045 on COPEs) eliminate the ~3.5\(\times\) conservativeness of analytical grf (FWER = 0.015), boosting subcortical cluster power from 18.0% (NS_GRF) and 24.0% (Raw Z) to 32.0–32.7% (doubling voxel sensitivity from 3.7% to 7.3–7.4%) and tripling lateral cortical power from 8.0% to 24.7% while maintaining zero false-positive leakage in null smooth DMN cortex.
  • Why nonstationary = TRUE should accompany empirical calibration: Using grf_sim with nonstationary = FALSE (Stat_GRFsim) slightly inflates smooth-zone false positives (FWER = 0.065, 2.7% smooth-DMN leakage) because large noise blobs in smooth cortex are scored against a single pooled global roughness; pairing nonstationary = TRUE with either sign_flip or grf_sim simultaneously achieves regional false-positive parity and nominal 0.05 whole-brain FWER.
  • When to prefer sign_flip vs. grf_sim: Whenever 4D residual or 4D subject copes are available, fwe_method = "sign_flip" is the recommended choice—it runs in ~1–7 seconds even on high-resolution 300k-voxel whole-brain masks (10\(\times\) faster than multi-scale 3D convolution) and adapts nonparametrically to empirical spatial correlation and heavy-tailed outlier structure (capturing Efron’s studentized self-normalization effect where Gaussian grf_sim becomes mildly conservative at 0.040). When only a 3D summary \(Z\)-map (with or without a 3D RPV map) is available, fwe_method = "grf_sim" achieves identical calibration accuracy without needing 4D volumes.

8 Algorithmic Architecture (Rcpp) & Benchmarks

Upstream pTFCE executed Nh = 100 full-volume 3D connected-component labeling sweeps (mmand::components) plus string-based frequency tables (base::table(ccc)) and allocated two 4D arrays (dim(img) x Nh).

In src/ptfce_core.cpp:

  • ptfce_tail_cpp(): Collects only in-mask voxels with \(Z > Z_{\text{estThr}}\) (~5–15% of total bounding-box voxels), sorts them once in descending order of intensity, and sweeps thresholds from high to low using a Disjoint-Set Union (Union-Find) structure with path compression and union-by-size. Voxel insertions and neighbor unions occur at most once per supra-threshold voxel across the entire run, making connected-component cost nearly independent of threshold density.
  • smoothest_cpp(): Performs three sequential, cache-contiguous passes over 4D res4d volumes without duplicating the 4D array in memory.
  • NullPtfceEngine (calibrate_fwer_grf_cpp / calibrate_fwer_signflip_cpp): Precomputes posterior normalization denominators once and populates a lazy 2D (threshold x log_cluster_mass) lookup table on demand, eliminating 100% of numerical Gauss–Kronrod quadrature inside the permutation/simulation loop and evaluating qnorm only once per replicate at the global maximum accumulator.
r4d_path <- system.file("extdata", "test03A_res4d.nii.gz", package = "pTFCE")
m3a_path <- system.file("extdata", "test03A_mask.nii.gz", package = "pTFCE")
r4d <- readNifti(r4d_path)
m3a <- readNifti(m3a_path)

t_sm3d  <- system.time(sm3 <- smoothest(z_nii, m_nii, verbose = FALSE))["elapsed"]
t_sm4d  <- system.time(sm4 <- smoothest(r4d, m3a, dof = 22, nonstationary = TRUE, verbose = FALSE))["elapsed"]
t_1s    <- system.time(ptfce(z_nii, m_nii, Rd = Rd, V = V, resels = sm3$resels,
                             Nh = 100, legacy = TRUE, verbose = FALSE))["elapsed"]
t_2s    <- system.time(ptfce(z_nii, m_nii, Rd = Rd, V = V, resels = sm3$resels,
                             sided = "two.sided", dh = 0.05, verbose = FALSE))["elapsed"]
t_2s_ns <- system.time(ptfce(z_nii, m3a, local_smoothness = sm4,
                             sided = "two.sided", dh = 0.05, nonstationary = TRUE, verbose = FALSE))["elapsed"]
set.seed(1)
t_sf200 <- system.time(ptfce(z_nii, m3a, residual = r4d, dof = 22, local_smoothness = sm4,
                             sided = "two.sided", nonstationary = TRUE,
                             fwe_method = "sign_flip", n_perm = 200L, verbose = FALSE))["elapsed"]

9 Usage & Migration Notes

9.1 Recommended Bi-Sided fMRI Workflows

library(pTFCE)

# 1. Recommended group-fMRI workflow: non-stationary bi-sided pTFCE + sign-flipping FWER
res <- ptfce(
  img = "zstat1.nii.gz",
  mask = "mask.nii.gz",
  residual = "res4d.nii.gz",   # or supply 4D subject contrasts via `copes = "copes4d.nii.gz"`
  dof = 42,
  sided = "two.sided",
  nonstationary = TRUE,
  fwe_method = "sign_flip",    # "grf" (default), "sign_flip", or "grf_sim"
  n_perm = 500L,
  connectivity = 6L,           # 6 (NN=1), 18 (NN=2), or 26 (NN=3)
  fwe_p = c(0.05, 0.01)
)

# 2. When only a 3D Z-map (plus optional RPV/local_smoothness) is available:
res_3d <- ptfce(
  img = "zstat1.nii.gz",
  mask = "mask.nii.gz",
  local_smoothness = "RPV.nii", # optional; omit for stationary smoothness
  sided = "two.sided",
  fwe_method = "grf_sim",
  n_perm = 500L
)

# 3. Reusing precomputed 4D local smoothness across multiple contrasts:
sm_ns <- smoothest("res4d.nii.gz", mask = "mask.nii.gz", dof = 42, nonstationary = TRUE)
res_cope1 <- ptfce("zstat1.nii.gz", mask = "mask.nii.gz", residual = "res4d.nii.gz", dof = 42,
                   local_smoothness = sm_ns, sided = "two.sided", fwe_method = "sign_flip")

# If starting from a t-statistic map instead of a Z-map:
z_img <- t2z("spmT_0001.nii.gz", dof = 42)

9.2 Known Statistical Properties & Remaining Future Directions

  1. Uncorrected voxelwise res$p vs. calibrated FWER thresholds: While fwe_method = "sign_flip" and fwe_method = "grf_sim" calibrate exact non-conservative FWER thresholds (res$fwer0.05.Z, res$fwe.Z, and empirical FWER \(p\)-values via (1 + sum(res$null_max_Z >= abs(z))) / (length(res$null_max_Z) + 1)), the uncorrected voxelwise res$p map remains mildly conservative in the moderate range (\(p \in [10^{-3}, 0.05]\)) due to \(H \ge Z_{\text{estThr}}\) truncation; thus naive Benjamini–Hochberg FDR on res$p remains conservative.
  2. Future enhancements:
    • Full Worsley (1996) 0D–3D resel vector (\(R_0, R_1, R_2, R_3\)): Accurate boundary/surface Euler characteristic FWER terms for analytical small-volume correction (SVC) and thin cortical ribbon ROIs when fwe_method = "grf" is used.
